title: 2018 AMC 12A Problem 6
statement: For positive integers \(m\) and \(n\) such that \(m + 10 \lt n + 1,\) both the mean and the median of the set \(\{m, m + 4, m + 10,\) \(n + 1,\) \(n + 2,\) \(2n\}\) are equal to \(n.\) What is \(m + n?\)

solutions.text:
Because \(m + 10 \lt n + 1,\) the six numbers are already increasing, so the median is the average of the middle two: \(\frac{(m+10)+(n+1)}{2} = n,\) giving \(m = n - 11.\) The mean condition is \[ \tiny \frac{(n-11)+(n-7)+(n-1)+(n+1)+(n+2)+2n}{6} = n, \] so \(7n - 16 = 6n\) and \(n = 16.\) Then \(m = 5,\) and \(m + n = 21.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The condition \(m + 10 \lt n + 1\) forces the six values to be listed in increasing order
Set the median \(\frac{(m+10)+(n+1)}{2} = n\) and set the mean equal to \(n,\) then solve the two equations
